title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: Local development committees are overseeing project implementation and driving skills development in the targeted states of North Kordufan and White Nile. (CAPISUD - SDN/16/01/BAD) Informal and formal Apprenticeship schemes are available to young people to gain skills on-the-job and facilitate their entry in the labour market. (CAPISUD) Tree facilitators and Master crafts person are capacitated to provide inclusive services and better training guidance. (CAPISUD) Post-training support, mentoring and coaching is provided to beneficiaries to fulfil potential in the labour market (CAPISUD) Coordination meetings with the key stakeholders as well as TREE committee leaders took place in the North Kordufan, White Nile state as well as in Khartoum. A total 830 enrolled apprentices, 699 of them in North Kordufan state and 131were reached in White Nile state. 1785 entrepreneurs were trained. 205 students trained in selected TVET Skills.940 men and women trained technical skills in goat/sheep rearing, fattening/breeding and cheese production.

description.narrative:
Ministerial counterparts’ capacity to design, develop, monitor, report, and close out SKILLS training programmes for rural and agriculturally dependent communities strengthened Local Skills Partners sustainability strategy developed to support the provision of agricultural skills training to rural and agriculturally dependent communities in PROSPECTS targeted locations of East Darfur and West Kordofan. Local skills and TVET Training Readiness Assessments conducted to provide inputs to (a) institutional capacity development and (b) piloting of a mobile containerized skills training workshop targeting rural and agricultural dependent communities in Assalaya, Keilak, and Muglad-Abyie localities. (PROSPECTS) Mainstreaming of social cohesion recommendations (2022 Social Cohesion Rapid Assessment) led to significant positive change in attitudinal survey findings over the SKILLS implementation phase of the PROSPECTS project. (Pending the release of Report) Learning and Training facilities are strengthened and revitalized through the procurement of instructional aides, classroom rehabilitation works, construction of latrines and sunshades, and enhancing facilities hygiene and cleanliness (PROSPECTS). The British Council recently sent in their training report for our training of counterpart Ministry staff. To date, 17 Ministry personnel completed training in Basic English Communication and will move on to Intermediate level training. 6 ministry staff completed Intermediate level language training and will now move on to Advanced language training. Technical specifications for vocational training equipment, beneficiary toolkits, productivity enhancing equipment, instructional aides and classroom maintenance supplies have cleared CO-ADD procurement and the project management team is working to prepare the ITBs, RFQs, and RFPs for national procurement.
The Rapid Social Cohesion Assessment was completed and presented to PROSPECTS partners in January and February of 2022. The key findings of the Report resulted in the reconfiguration of the SKILLS component, the initiation of a pilot community based land use planning initiative with FAO, and the inclusion of a borehole water management committee for EIIP civil works.
